archetype.name: Lost Season (a step backward)
archetype.definition: After climbing from 50 wins in 2023 to 76 in 2025, the Athletics gave back 12 wins, finished with the league's worst run differential, and were saved from last place in the West only by the Angels.

report.headline: A 16-10 April, then run prevention collapsed and erased 2025's progress

recap.finish: 64-98, fourth in the AL West, 17 games behind Houston; missed the postseason
recap.body:
The 2026 Athletics could hit a little and could not stop anyone. Their .719 OPS ranked 15th, squarely average, though runs per game ranked only 20th. On the other side, a 5.51 ERA ranked 29th, run prevention ranked 29th, and the fielders cost 40.7 runs, also 29th. Net, they were outscored by 1.47 runs a game, dead last in the league and about 238 runs over the season. The grades agree: D- for the hitters, D- for the rotation, D+ for the bullpen.

April was the false dawn. They went 16-10 while scoring 115 and allowing 114, a team getting by on the margins rather than beating people. Even by the end of May they were 28-31. The slide was gradual until July, when it stopped being gradual: 5-19 with 87 runs scored and 163 allowed, then 8-20 in August. Across those two months they went 13-39, were outscored by 133 runs, and somewhere in the summer had a 10-game losing streak. September at 11-13 was only a little better, and the final ten games went 3-7, including 1-10, 2-13 and 0-9 losses.

The lineup had a real core. Nick Kurtz posted a 138 wRC+ with a .396 OBP in 99 games and made the All-Star team. Shea Langeliers hit 23 homers with a 115 wRC+ and ranks 3rd among 78 catchers on the site. Zack Gelof hit 22 homers and was worth 2.7 WAR, and Henry Bolte led the team at 2.8 WAR with 21 steals. The problem was where the playing time went. Lawrence Butler (539 PA, 96 wRC+, -10.9 Def Runs) and Jeff McNeil (520 PA, 83 wRC+) took the most plate appearances on the club and were worth roughly nothing. Jonah Heim's 66 wRC+ over 390 PA was a hole. Kurtz and Soderstrom both ended the year on the 60-day injured list.

The rotation was where the season was lost. Jeffrey Springs threw the most innings, 142.2, with a 6.18 ERA and a 6.02 FIP that says the results were earned, not unlucky. Jacob Lopez added 123.1 innings at 5.47. J.T. Ginn (3.71 ERA, 1.7 WAR) was the one dependable starter, and he and Luis Severino finished on the 60-day IL. Walks ran high almost everywhere: every starter and every leading reliever walked at least 9% of batters, and closer Hogan Harris walked 13.5%. Jack Perkins soaked up 121 relief innings at a 6.10 ERA, and behind it all sat a defense that took away hits nobody could afford to give.

The 64 wins actually flatter them. The W vs Run Diff figure of +4.2 ranks 5th in the league, so a run differential this bad usually produces closer to 60 wins. Compared with 2025, the hitting slipped a bit (OPS .749 to .719, offense 12th to 20th). The run prevention fell apart: ERA rose from 4.70 to 5.51 and Fielding Runs from -5.3 to -40.7. That gap, more than the bats, is the story of the year.

highlights.title: A young offensive core that produced
highlights.body: Kurtz, Langeliers, Gelof, Bolte and Soderstrom all posted a wRC+ between 111 and 138, and two of them made the All-Star team. This is production spread across several players, not one hot bat, which makes it the most durable thing on the roster. The caveat is availability: Kurtz played only 99 games and Soderstrom 109, and both ended on the 60-day IL.

highlights.title: Ginn and Jump give the rotation something
highlights.body: J.T. Ginn's 3.71 ERA over 138.1 innings was the only above-average starting line on the staff. Gage Jump's 5.47 ERA hides a 4.01 FIP and a 24.7% strikeout rate, which points to better results with any help from the defense. Of the two, Jump's underlying numbers are the more encouraging.

highlights.title: Medina and Harris held the late innings
highlights.body: Luis Medina (3.08 ERA, 29.3% K) and Hogan Harris (3.33 ERA, 17 saves, 13 holds) helped make the bullpen the best-graded group, even if that grade is only a D+. Both miss bats, but both also walked more than 12% of hitters, so their run prevention rests on thin margins.

lowlights.title: Run prevention near the bottom
lowlights.body: A 5.51 team ERA ranked 29th, and the starter with the most innings, Springs, had a 6.18 ERA backed by a 6.02 FIP. High walk rates ran through the whole staff, so this was a pitching problem first, not just bad defense behind good pitchers. It is the reason a middle-of-the-pack OPS turned into the league's worst run differential.

lowlights.title: A defense that gave runs away
lowlights.body: Fielding Runs of -40.7 ranked 29th and were the worst of the six seasons on the sheet. Corner outfielders Butler (-10.9) and Cortes (-6.5) led the damage, with Soderstrom, Heim and McNeil adding to it. That is a large swing from -5.3 in 2025, and it makes every pitcher on the staff look worse.

lowlights.title: The July-August collapse
lowlights.body: After a 16-10 April, the team went 5-19 in July and 8-20 in August, allowing 6.8 and 6.2 runs a game. Even the 64-win total overstates the club, given a +4.2 W vs Run Diff. The summer looks like the roster's true level showing through rather than a fluky slump.

arc.note: A 16-10 April briefly suggested 2025's climb would continue. The team then lost steadily through May and June, bottomed out at 13-39 across July and August, and was 3-7 over its final ten games.

recap.nextYear: The bats are the foundation. Kurtz, Langeliers, Gelof, Bolte and Soderstrom were all above average, so the lineup's job is to stay healthy and stop handing 1,000-plus plate appearances to below-average bats like Butler, McNeil and Heim. The rotation needs the most work: beyond Ginn and the strikeout-driven Jump, the innings went to arms who were genuinely bad, and walks were a staff-wide issue. The 2025 to 2026 fielding swing was huge, and improving it is probably the cheapest path back toward 2025's level. Expect no help from luck. The +4.2 W vs Run Diff means this team played closer to a 60-win level, so a similar roster would likely win fewer games, not more.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; trends agree across months, grades and run differential.
